_comment: Light fixtures and their switches. Units: DECIMAL FEET, same frame as floorplan.json.
_why: Lighting is defined as data for the same reason the walls are: horror events need to address lights by name and by group ('turn off everything downstairs', 'the porch light is on again'), and that is only possible if every fixture has a stable identity rather than being a hand-placed object someone renamed.
_kelvin: Colour temperature in kelvin. Domestic bulbs are 2400-3000K and read as warm and yellow; 4000K+ reads as institutional and is deliberately reserved for the garage and laundry, where it feels colder and less welcoming than the rest of the house.
_intensity: Unity light intensity. Values here are tuned for a dark scene - the house should be lit in pools with real darkness between them, not evenly flooded. Raising these to make the house readable is almost always the wrong fix; raise the Moonlight or the grade's post-exposure instead.
_groups: A switch toggles a GROUP, not a fixture, so one switch can control several lights. Group names are free text; reuse one across rooms to gang them together.
_oneFittingPerRoom: Cut from 30 fittings to 21 after an audit. An ordinary room has ONE ceiling light, not two or three - a second fitting reads as a shop or an office, and each one also costs a real-time shadow map every frame it is lit. Extras now have to justify themselves: the pendant over the dining table and the two exterior lights do, a second light in the middle of the kitchen does not.

_switchesComment: Switches sit on a wall inside the room at 4'-0", the standard height. 'controls' is a group name from above. Stage 7's interaction system will drive these; for now they can be toggled from code.
_switchPlacement: Every one of these was re-derived from where the DOOR actually is, after an audit found five switches hanging in open thresholds with no wall behind them and four more sitting inside their own doorway. A switch belongs on solid wall, beside the door you enter by, on the latch side so the opening door does not sweep across it. Check both when moving one: is there a wall here, and is it clear of the door swing?
